success_patterns: Every success named the slot type first (person, work, holiday, drink, toy, sitcom) and answered with a bare entity of that type, never an anchor from the clue (e.g. 'author of Gai-Jin' -> James Clavell, 'sitcom' -> Welcome Back, Kotter, 'singer' -> Alice Cooper).

Two tasks had a verbatim archive line ('clue | Answer. right: Name' or 'clue | Welcome Back, Kotter.'). The agent copied the answer as printed, stripping only the contestant tag and trailing period, and kept punctuation such as the comma.

Where passages repeated the clue's facts across many independent pages (Slinky, Rikki-Tikki-Tavi, Alice Cooper), the agent took the entity that recurred with all the clue's details and kept the standard hyphenated or short form.

Clue fragments that give an old or alternate name ('...as the U.S. holiday Decoration Day') were solved by finding passages that say 'originally called / formerly known as <clue name>' and answering with the other, current name (Memorial Day), not the clue's own phrase.

When the retrieved passages were noisy keyword matches (foreign-language pages, product pages), the agent used its own knowledge of the jargon (doux/brut) to pick the category (champagne). It used the one glossary passage as confirmation and answered with the bare generic noun.

Pun or wordplay clues ('no flash in the Tai-Pan') were treated as decoration. The agent answered from the factual core (author of Gai-Jin), and the other work titles named in the clue confirmed the same author.

patch.reasoning: Most successes already follow existing rules (type-check, verbatim archive copy, bare form). Two patterns are not stated explicitly. First, a leading-ellipsis fragment that names an old or alias name asks for the standard name on the other side of 'originally called / formerly known as'. This is one of the clue shapes most prone to echoing the clue phrase. Second, when passages are keyword noise, jargon in the clue should be resolved with the agent's own knowledge and confirmed by any glossary passage. Both edits are small, extend existing bullets, and do not touch Rule 3 or the formatting rules.

edits.target: - If the clue is a fragment, work out what single thing connects it to the context.
edits.content: - A fragment that begins with '...' and names an old, alternate or local name ('...as the U.S. holiday Decoration Day') asks for the OTHER name of the same thing. Find the passages that say 'originally called / formerly known as / also called <clue name>' and answer with the name they pair it with (the current standard name). Never answer with the clue's own name.

edits.target: - Make sure your answer fits every detail (year, role, action), not just the topic.
edits.content: - Noisy passages (keyword matches from foreign-language, product or unrelated pages) with a jargon clue ('grades range from doux to brut'): decide the category from your own knowledge of the terms, confirm it with any glossary or topical passage, and answer with the bare common noun of that category ('Champagne'). Ignore pages that only share a stray word with the clue.
